record.paper_title: Some problems and conjectures about L2-invariants
record.original_question: Let G be a discrete group, let G = G_0 ⊇ G_1 ⊇ G_2 ⊇ ... be a finite-index normal chain with trivial intersection, let p: X̃ → X be a G-covering, and let α be a classical invariant such as the Euler characteristic, signature, Betti numbers over Q or F_p, Reidemeister or Ray-Singer torsion, or logarithmic torsion homology size. Does the normalized sequence α(X[i])/[G:G_i] always converge? If it converges, is the limit independent of the chain {G_i}? If both answers are yes, is the limit always the corresponding L2-analogue α^{(2)}(X; N(G))?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.1 (Approximation Problem). (1) Does the sequence converge? (2) If yes, is the limit independent of the chain {Gi}? (3) If yes, what is the limit? The hope is that the answer to the first two questions is yes and the limit turns out to be an L2-analogue α(2) of α applied to the G-space X, i.e., one can prove an equality of the type lim i→∞ α(X[i])/[G : Gi] = α(2)(X; N (G)).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a discrete (countable) group and let
$$G = G_0 \supseteq G_1 \supseteq G_2 \supseteq \cdots$$
be a descending chain of normal subgroups of finite index in $G$ with trivial intersection $\bigcap_{i\ge 0} G_i = \{1\}$. Let $p\colon \widetilde X \to X$ be a regular $G$-covering of a finite connected CW-complex (or compact Riemannian manifold) $X$, and for each $i\ge 0$ let $X[i] := G_i \backslash \widetilde X$ denote the finite covering of $X$ associated with $G_i$, so that $[G:G_i]$ is the degree of $X[i]\to X$.

Let $\alpha$ be a classical numerical invariant of finite CW-complexes (or of compact manifolds), e.g.
- the Euler characteristic $\chi$,
- the signature $\mathrm{sign}$,
- the rational Betti numbers $b_n(-;\mathbb{Q})$,
- the mod-$p$ Betti numbers $b_n(-;\mathbb{F}_p)$ for a prime $p$,
- Reidemeister torsion,
- Ray–Singer analytic torsion,
- the logarithmic size of the torsion subgroup of integral homology $\log |H_n(-;\mathbb{Z})_{\mathrm{tors}}|$.

For each such invariant there is a corresponding $L^2$-analogue $\alpha^{(2)}(\widetilde X; \mathcal N(G))$ defined via the group von Neumann algebra $\mathcal N(G)$ (e.g.\ $L^2$-Betti numbers $b_n^{(2)}$, $L^2$-torsion $\rho^{(2)}$, etc.).

Answer the following three questions:

(1) Does the normalized sequence
$$\frac{\alpha(X[i])}{[G:G_i]}$$
converge as $i\to\infty$?

(2) If it converges, is the limit independent of the chosen finite-index normal chain $\{G_i\}$ with trivial intersection?

(3) If yes to both, is the limit always equal to the corresponding $L^2$-invariant, i.e.
$$\lim_{i\to\infty}\frac{\alpha(X[i])}{[G:G_i]} = \alpha^{(2)}(\widetilde X; \mathcal N(G))\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The approximation problem is fully solved for $L^2$-Betti numbers (Lück's approximation theorem, 1994) and has been extended substantially (e.g. to sofic groups by Elek–Szabó and to broader chains). The Euler characteristic case is trivial and the signature case is settled. However, for mod-$p$ Betti numbers, Reidemeister/Ray–Singer torsion, and torsion homology growth, the problem is widely open in general; partial results exist (e.g. amenable groups, locally symmetric spaces, the Bergeron–Venkatesh conjecture, the determinant conjecture for sofic groups), but the general approximation conjecture for $L^2$-torsion and torsion growth remains open.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on L2-torsion (Lück)
status_evidence.snippet: The torsion approximation conjecture splits into several intriguing and wide open problems; it is known in special cases but open in general.
status_evidence.claim: Torsion approximation is open in general but known in special cases.

status_evidence.title: L2-torsion, the measure-theoretic determinant conjecture, and uniform measure equivalence
status_evidence.snippet: Determinant conjecture is known for sofic groups; Szegő-type theorem on amenable groups confirms vanishing of L2-torsion for amenable groups with finite classifying space.
status_evidence.claim: Approximation/determinant results are established for sofic and amenable groups.

status_evidence.title: Classical torsion and L2-torsion (Lück)
status_evidence.snippet: For locally symmetric spaces the torsion approximation reduces to the Bergeron–Venkatesh conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Connections to Bergeron–Venkatesh; problem largely open.
